extra.message: Pickle deserialization of untrusted request body — Remote code execution on the server via crafted pickle payload [verified: pickle.loads on raw request body reachable behind only a static shared-secret header, which the threat model explicitly treats as a weak gate.]
Server-side template injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template built from request input — Arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 SSTI gadget chains [verified: Same Jinja2 SSTI sink as idx5/18.]
OS command injection in ping probe endpoint — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server [verified: Same os.system shell injection sink as idx2/16.]

IDOR on matter detail API — Cross-tenant disclosure of privileged matter metadata (sensitivity level, client identity, description) to any staff user regardless of case assignment [verified: api_matter_detail only blocks clients via is_client() but performs an unscoped get_object_or_404(Matter, pk=pk), unlike api_matters which filters by lead_attorney/paralegals — any attorney/paralegal can enumerate pks to read matters they're not assigned to.]

Cross-tenant document exposure in api_documents (missing client-ownership scope) — Any authenticated client user can list documents (titles, categories, matter linkage) belonging to other clients' legal matters, leaking confidential case metadata across tenants and letting an attacker discover document/matter IDs to pivot into further IDOR requests. [verified: api_documents filters only by visibility='client_shared' for client-role users with no check tying the document's matter/client to the requesting user, unlike documents/views.py's can_access_document which enforces doc.matter.client_id == client.pk.]

IDOR via email-based client-matter lookup after self-service email change — Cross-tenant disclosure of another client's legal matters (case status, practice area, lead attorney) by impersonating their email address [verified: clients/views.py:95 resolves the client record solely via Client.objects.get(email=request.user.email); ProfileUpdateForm (accounts/forms.py:11-20) lets any authenticated user change their own email to any value with no uniqueness or verification check, so a client can set their email to match another client's and hit /clients/my-matters/ to view that client's matters.]
Code injection via eval() of user-supplied expression — Arbitrary code execution by escaping the restricted eval sandbox [verified: Same eval() sandbox-bypass sink as idx1/17.]

Insecure CORS configuration reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the JSON response, leading to cross-site data theft [verified: Same reflected-Origin CORS-with-credentials sink as idx7/22.]

CORS misconfiguration reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can perform credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses [verified: Same reflected-Origin CORS-with-credentials sink as idx7/22/35.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution and DTD loading enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service via crafted XML with external/internal entities [verified: Same XXE-enabled parser sink as idx4/19.]

NoSQL injection via unvalidated MongoDB filter passthrough — Bypass intended query constraints, extract arbitrary records, or leverage $where for server-side JS execution [verified: Same unsanitized Mongo filter passthrough as idx3/20.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure and/or SSRF via crafted XML with external entities [verified: lxml XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False parsing raw request body enables classic XXE.]
XXE via lxml parser with DTD/entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure and SSRF via XML external entities [verified: Same XXE-enabled lxml parser sink as idx4/19/33.]

IDOR allows creating (and auto-approving) client messages on unassigned matters — Any attorney can author and self-approve a client-visible message on a matter they are not assigned to, allowing unauthorized communication to another attorney's client. [verified: client_message_create only checks !is_client() at views.py:39, no matter-assignment scoping; attorney/firm_admin path (52-56) auto-approves and sets is_client_visible=True with no ownership check.]

IDOR allows approving client messages on unassigned matters — An attorney with approval rights can approve/publish client-visible messages belonging to matters they do not own, exposing unvetted content to a client. [verified: client_message_approve (views.py:70-73) checks only global can_approve_messages(), never msg.matter assignment, allowing cross-matter approval and client-visible publication.]

Missing authorization on client message send endpoint — Any authenticated user (including clients) can force delivery/visibility state changes on client messages belonging to other matters, undermining the attorney approval workflow for client communications [verified: client_message_send only checks msg.status=='approved' with no role/ownership check, unlike client_message_approve which requires can_approve_messages(); any logged-in user including clients can flip status to 'sent' for any matter's message.]

Missing brute-force protection on login endpoint — Attackers can perform unlimited online password-guessing/credential-stuffing against any account, including privileged firm_admin/attorney accounts with access to privileged client data. [verified: CustomLoginView uses Django's default AuthenticationForm/LoginView with no django-axes/ratelimit or lockout logic anywhere in settings.py or views.py, allowing unlimited password guesses per account.]

CSRF via state-changing GET request on user_toggle_active — An attacker can force an authenticated firm_admin to unknowingly disable or re-enable any user account (including other admins), causing account tampering or denial of service. [verified: user_toggle_active has no request.method check, so a plain GET (e.g. via tag) toggles any user's active status, and Django's CSRF middleware does not protect GET requests.]

IDOR: deadline creation not scoped to attorney/paralegal's own matters — An attorney or paralegal can create deadlines (and leak knowledge of matter existence, timing, descriptions) for cases outside their assignment, polluting another attorney's docket or planting a bogus deadline in an unrelated client matter [verified: deadline_create only checks is_client() then binds DeadlineForm with unrestricted ModelForm queryset for 'matter' (forms.py:8), letting any attorney/paralegal create deadlines on matters they aren't assigned to.]

Mass assignment: deadline 'matter' field re-assignable to any matter without scope check — Authorized editors can move a deadline's matter association to any matter in the system, bypassing per-matter access scoping and corrupting docket/deadline integrity for other users' cases [verified: deadline_edit authorizes via can_edit_deadline on the deadline's current matter, but binds the same DeadlineForm allowing 'matter' reassignment to any Matter id with no scope check, so an authorized editor can move the deadline off/onto arbitrary matters.]

CSRF via state-changing GET on deadline_complete — An attacker can forge a cross-site GET request that marks a legal deadline as completed, corrupting deadline-tracking integrity which is critical to legal outcomes. [verified: deadline_complete mutates status/completed_at on any GET with no method check or CSRF token requirement, matching the confirmed pattern elsewhere; login_required does not prevent cross-site forged navigation from an authenticated session.]

Missing authentication on internal ops endpoint exposing client PII summary — Unauthenticated disclosure of aggregate client/case sensitive business data [verified: Confirms idx8 — no _wrk_gate call, unauthenticated disclosure of case counts and ops_memo.]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Phishing via trusted-domain redirect to attacker site [verified: redirect(lane) uses the raw 'lane' param with no allow-list or same-origin check, enabling open redirect.]

Sensitive Authorization header and body logged in plaintext — Bearer tokens and sensitive request content are exposed to anyone with log access, enabling credential theft [verified: Same plaintext Authorization/body logging as idx10/23.]

TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound partner request — Man-in-the-middle attacker can intercept or tamper with outbound requests/responses to the partner endpoint [verified: Same disabled TLS verification as idx12/26.]

TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept/tamper with outbound HTTPS traffic [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() used for an outbound HTTPS request disables certificate validation, enabling MITM on that traffic.]
Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attacker can intercept/tamper with partner communications [verified: Same disabled TLS verification issue as idx12.]

IDOR allows privileged notes on unassigned matters — A staff user with note-writing privilege can attach privileged attorney-client notes to any matter in the firm, not just their own assigned cases, polluting privileged records outside their case team [verified: privileged_note_create checks only the role-based can_write_privileged_notes() and never verifies the user is assigned to the resolved matter, unlike other views (api_matters) that check lead_attorney/paralegals; any privileged-role staff can attach notes to any matter.]

CSRF via state-changing GET on notification_mark_read — Attacker-forced GET request can alter another user's notification state cross-site; low severity impact but same missing state-changing-request control class. [verified: notification_mark_read has no @require_POST/method check, so a GET request (e.g. via a cross-site tag) flips is_read for a notification scoped to the requesting user, consistent with the confirmed pattern at user_toggle_active.]

Audit log IP attribution spoofable via unvalidated X-Forwarded-For header — Attacker can forge the source IP recorded against their own actions in the audit trail (e.g. document downloads, client record deletions, role changes), destroying the tamper-evidence/forensic value of the audit log — a core asset per the threat model — and potentially misdirecting incident response toward an innocent IP. [verified: XFF is trusted unconditionally with no proxy validation (no SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER/trusted-proxy check in settings), so any direct client can spoof the IP recorded in AuditLog rows.]

Unauthorized-access path in audit_log_list raises NameError due to missing import — Reliable crash for any non-firm-admin user probing the audit log endpoint; combined with DEBUG=True (misconfiguration elsewhere) this discloses internal stack traces, file paths, and settings to unprivileged authenticated users. [verified: redirect is genuinely unimported while called on the access-denied path for any non-firm-admin user, causing a NameError/500; DEBUG is env-controlled and defaults False so info-disclosure impact is conditional, but the crash/DoS-of-endpoint itself is confirmed.]

Unrestricted file upload with no content/type validation — Arbitrary file placement on server disk; potential follow-on execution if served or included [verified: Uploaded file saved via FileSystemStorage.save with no extension/content-type/size validation, though gated behind weak static header; no path traversal but unrestricted file type is real given no validation logic at all.]

Unbounded resource allocation in case_spool_fan_315 — Attacker-controlled DoS via memory/CPU exhaustion, potentially crashing the worker process and affecting availability for legitimate legal-case users [verified: count query param passed unbounded into range(count) with no upper-bound check, allowing large memory/CPU allocation; gated but still a real missing bound check.]
Verbose error response leaking internal filesystem path — Disclosure of internal server directory structure aiding further attacks [verified: Same internal path disclosure via str(exc) as idx14.]

Verbose error response leaks internal filesystem path — Discloses internal server directory structure aiding further attacks [verified: str(exc) embeds the internal BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path and is returned directly in the JSON error response.]

Hardcoded weak verifier secrets with no brute-force protection — Attacker can brute-force the 4-digit verifier codes to pass the identity check, and hardcoded secrets in source risk broader compromise [verified: Hardcoded 4-digit verifier dict with plain equality check and no rate limiting allows brute-force guessing once behind the ops gate; low severity since gated but genuinely absent control.]

Security headers deliberately weakened — Removes defense-in-depth browser protections, increasing exploitability of any XSS elsewhere [verified: Response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to 0 and empties CSP — genuine weakening of security headers on a reachable endpoint.]

Security headers deliberately disabled (CSP emptied, XSS protection disabled) — Removes defense-in-depth protections against XSS/clickjacking for responses served through this endpoint [verified: Same disabled security headers as idx11/28.]

Weak PRNG used for nonce/code generation — Predictable tokens/nonces can be brute-forced or guessed, undermining any authentication/verification use [verified: Same weak-PRNG nonce generation as idx13/25.]

Internal configuration and filesystem path disclosure — Attacker learns internal Django settings module name and absolute server-side export directory path, aiding further targeted attacks (e.g. crafting path-traversal or settings-module override payloads) [verified: Returns DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR path directly in JSON response, disclosing internal deployment/filesystem layout.]

CSV formula injection (CSV import feeding CSV export) enables spreadsheet code execution — Attacker-controlled data stored via CSV import is later exported unsanitized; opening the exported file in Excel/Google Sheets executes an embedded formula (e.g. DDE) against the firm_admin's machine, enabling client-side code execution or data exfiltration from the admin's workstation. [verified: csv.writer writes free-text fields (title, name, tags, etc.) with no escaping of leading =/+/-/@ characters, and import_clients_csv/import_matters_csv store arbitrary CSV content unvalidated, so injected formulas round-trip to export files. Severity is low since the attack requires a firm_admin (already trusted/privileged) to import malicious data and only harms the admin's own workstation on open]

CSV formula injection in export_deadlines_csv — An attacker who controls a deadline/matter title can embed a spreadsheet formula that executes when a firm admin opens the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets, potentially leading to further compromise or data exfiltration via DDE/formula execution. [verified: dl.title and dl.matter.title are user-settable free text written raw into CSV cells with no leading =/+/-/@ sanitization, matching the already-confirmed pattern at views.py:42.]

CSV formula injection in export_documents_csv — An attacker-controlled document title/tag containing a leading formula character executes as a spreadsheet formula when the exported CSV is opened by staff. [verified: doc.title and doc.tags are attacker-influenceable fields written unsanitized into CSV cells, same missing-sanitization pattern as the confirmed finding.]
